stories.headline: Iran claims Bahrain radar strike after Trump says no deal needed
stories.question: Is the US–Iran war spreading across the Gulf now that Trump says no deal is needed?
stories.dek: There are signs it is. Iran claims its first direct hit on a US military site in months, in Bahrain, and the Houthis claim Saudi oil strikes. Neither is confirmed, but oil prices jumped.

so_far.text: The war began on 28 February 2026, when Israel and the US attacked Iran and killed Supreme Leader Ali Khamenei. Iran struck Israel and Gulf states. It also claimed control of the Strait of Hormuz, the narrow sea route out of the Gulf. A ceasefire began on 7 April. An interim deal followed on 17 June. In July the US reinstated oil sanctions, and on 8 July Trump declared the ceasefire "over". Vice President JD Vance later renewed efforts to end the war, now eight months old.

what_happened.text: On 12 November Trump posted: "We don't need a deal with Iran." He said the US has Iran's money, "Hundreds of Billions of Dollars", and "their Strait". The FT reported that this signalled an end to Vance's peace push. On 13 November Al Jazeera reported a claim by Iran's Revolutionary Guard (IRGC). The IRGC said it destroyed a US early-warning radar in Bahrain. It called this an answer to a US air strike on a telecoms tower in Sirik, southern Iran. US Central Command said it shot down two IRGC drones and reported no damage. On 12 November Yemen's Houthis claimed strikes on Saudi oil sites.

steps.text: On 12 November Trump said the US needs no deal. The FT reported this signalled an end to Vance's peace push.
The US struck a telecoms tower at Sirik, which overlooks Hormuz. Iran answered by claiming it destroyed a US radar in Bahrain.
Iran claims a hit on a radar in Bahrain, a Gulf host country. CENTCOM says it downed two drones and reported no damage.
With Hormuz contested, Saudi oil reportedly goes around it by pipeline. The Houthis claim they hit that pipeline and the Yanbu oil facility.
Threats to both oil exits raise fears of lost supply. So oil prices and airlines react before any damage is confirmed.

history.text:
This story goes back decades. In 1953 a coup backed by the US and Britain removed Iran's prime minister, Mosaddegh. In 1979 a revolution created the Islamic republic, and ties with the US were cut.

In 2002 Iran's nuclear programme was revealed. A nuclear deal on that programme, the JCPOA, was agreed in 2015. The US left it in 2018 and reimposed sanctions.

In June 2025 Israel attacked Iranian nuclear and military sites, and the US struck Iranian nuclear facilities. A ceasefire ended this "Twelve-Day War". UN sanctions returned in September 2025.

On 28 February 2026 the US and Israel attacked again and killed Supreme Leader Ali Khamenei. Iran hit Israel and Gulf states and claimed control of the Strait of Hormuz, the sea route out of the Gulf. A two-week ceasefire began on 7 April. Vance led talks in Islamabad, and they failed on 12 April. On 13 April Trump announced a blockade of Iranian ports. On 17 June an interim deal required Iran to dilute its highly enriched uranium, and the US waived sanctions so Iran could sell oil. On 7 July Iran was accused of striking three ships in Hormuz. The US struck dozens of targets and reinstated oil sanctions. On 8 July Trump declared the ceasefire "over".

Lower-confidence sources (Wikipedia and AGBI) say Yemen's Houthis widened the war towards Saudi Arabia. They declared a naval blockade on Saudi Arabia in July. In September they started a crisis at Bab al-Mandab, the strait beside Yemen. In October they attacked Saudi Arabia.

analogy.text: Think of a shop with a main gate and a back door. The main gate (Hormuz) is jammed, so goods leave through the back door (Saudi Arabia's pipeline to the Red Sea). Now someone throws stones at the back door. Before anyone checks for damage, buyers rush to stock up.

lesson.concept: How oil escapes when Hormuz is blocked
lesson.big_idea: Gulf oil normally leaves by sea through the Strait of Hormuz. When that door is blocked, Saudi Arabia can pipe some oil across to the Red Sea. Attacking that side door squeezes what is left, so prices jump.

steps.title: Hormuz is the main door
steps.text: The Strait of Hormuz is a narrow sea passage between Iran and Oman. Tankers carrying Gulf oil sail through it. Since 28 February 2026 Iran has claimed control of it, so this main door is no longer reliable.

steps.title: A pipeline is a side door
steps.text: A pipeline carries oil overland instead of by sea. Saudi Arabia's East-West pipeline runs from its eastern oil fields to Yanbu, a port on the Red Sea. Saudi Arabia has reportedly been using it to send oil around Hormuz.

steps.title: The side door has weak points
steps.text: Pumping stations push oil along a pipeline, and if one stops, the flow slows. Ships leaving Yanbu may also pass Bab al-Mandab, the strait beside Yemen. Reports say the Houthis started a crisis there in September 2026.

steps.title: Fewer doors, higher price
steps.text: Traders pay more when they fear barrels may not arrive, even before any damage is confirmed. After the Houthis claimed attacks on Saudi sites, Brent crude rose 3.3% on 12 November.

example.setup: Imagine a country that sells 10 barrels of oil a day. Normally 8 leave by the sea route and 2 by pipeline. Assume the pipeline can carry at most 5 barrels.

lines.label: Normal day
lines.note: Both doors are open, so everything gets out.

lines.label: Sea route shut
lines.note: Half the oil is now stuck at home.

lines.label: Pumping station hit
lines.calc: Assume pipeline falls from 5 to 3 barrels
lines.note: One hit on the only open door.

lines.label: Total stuck
lines.note: Seven in ten barrels cannot reach buyers.

lines.label: Share lost to the hit
lines.note: A small hit removes a big share of what was left.

example.result: With the main door shut, every barrel depends on the side door. One hit there cuts 40% of what was still flowing. That is why buyers worry and prices rise.

apply.text: This is the squeeze traders now fear. Iran has claimed control of Hormuz since February, and Saudi Arabia reportedly sends oil around it by pipeline. On 12 November the Houthis claimed hits on Pumping Station No. 7 and on Yanbu. Saudi damage is not confirmed, yet Brent rose 3.3% to $95.82 that day.

practice.q: Same country, but assume the pipeline can carry 6 barrels and an attack cuts its flow by a third. How many barrels get out?
practice.answer: The sea route is shut, so only the pipeline works: 6 barrels. A third of 6 is 2. 6 − 2 = 4 barrels get out. A normal day sends 10, so 6 barrels are stuck.

check.q: Why did Houthi claims about a Saudi pipeline push oil prices up when no damage was confirmed?
options: The pipeline reportedly lets Saudi oil bypass Hormuz, so a threat to it endangers one of the last open exits

The US confirmed that the pipeline was destroyed
check.why: With Hormuz contested, the pipeline is a key side door. A threat to it raises fears of lost supply, even before damage is confirmed.

thread.previously: The third round of US-mediated Russia–Ukraine talks in Abu Dhabi (10–11 November 2026) ended without a breakthrough. A large prisoner exchange was agreed, with no number or date given. The BBC says talks centred on Europe's post-war security framework. The Kremlin demands talks on European security structures; the US urged Russia to include Europe and cited a lack of trust. Trump's envoys said they would go to Moscow; the BBC says envoys meet Putin and Zelensky on 12 November.
thread.changed: The envoys met Putin in Moscow and Zelensky near Dublin on 12 November. Kushner says the biggest prisoner swap of the war is finalised. Europe named a five-country team; Moscow has not agreed to include it.

stories.headline: US envoys see Putin and Zelensky: prisoner swap, no ceasefire
stories.question: What came out of the US envoys' meetings with Putin and Zelensky?
stories.dek: The envoys finalised the war's biggest prisoner swap and promised a new three-way round, possibly with Europe at the table. There is still no ceasefire, no date and no shift on territory.

so_far.text: Direct Russia–Ukraine talks restarted in Istanbul on 16 May 2025, the first since 2022. US-brokered talks in Geneva on 18 February 2026 reportedly collapsed after about two hours. On 10–11 November 2026, Russia, Ukraine and the US met together in Abu Dhabi. Kremlin aide Yuri Ushakov said both Moscow and Washington saw those contacts as constructive. The next day, 12 November, the US envoys met Putin in Moscow.

what_happened.text: On 12 November 2026, US envoys Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner met Vladimir Putin in Moscow. That evening they met Volodymyr Zelensky at Baldonnel, in west Dublin. Witkoff said progress was made and a new three-way meeting is set, but gave no date. Kremlin aide Yuri Ushakov called the Putin talks 'substantive, constructive, frank, and useful'. Zelensky said the visit brought 'real results': Russia accepted what would be the biggest prisoner exchange of the war. Kushner said it was finalised. No number or date was given. No ceasefire was mentioned.

steps.text: Russia and Ukraine distrust each other, so the US carries offers between them and hosts joint rounds.
Small, checkable steps like a prisoner swap come first, because each side can see the other deliver.
The hardest issue has not moved: Putin still demands territory Russia claims to have annexed and rejects foreign peacekeepers.
Kushner says no deal is possible without Europe; Moscow resists Europeans in direct talks because they fund and arm Ukraine.
Yet Moscow also wants a new European security system, so Europe's seat is both a hurdle and a Russian demand.

history.text:
The story begins in 2014. In February that year, unmarked Russian troops occupied Crimea. In March, Russia annexed it. In April 2014, Russian-backed militants seized towns in Donbas, in Ukraine's east. They proclaimed the Donetsk and Luhansk 'People's Republics', and a war began there.

In February 2015 the Minsk II agreement was signed to end that war. It was never fully carried out, and the front line largely froze. That pattern matters for the current talks: a signed paper without follow-through did not bring peace.

On 24 February 2022, Russia launched a full-scale invasion of Ukraine. In September 2022, it declared that four provinces were now Russian: Donetsk, Luhansk, Kherson and Zaporizhzhia. The UN General Assembly condemned this. These claims are still the core of the territorial dispute, and the hardest thing to negotiate.

Talks came slowly. Russia and Ukraine met directly in Istanbul on 16 May 2025, for the first time since 2022. The US then stepped in as broker. After a round in Abu Dhabi, US-brokered talks in Geneva on 18 February 2026 reportedly collapsed after about two hours. The sides met again in Abu Dhabi on 10–11 November 2026. That round led to the envoys' visits to Putin and Zelensky on 12 November.

lesson.concept: How a mediator builds a deal between enemies
lesson.big_idea: A mediator helps enemies who don't trust each other by carrying offers between them, then bringing them into one room. Every extra party at the table adds more agreements that must hold.

steps.title: A go-between carries messages
steps.text: When two sides at war don't trust each other, a third party, called the mediator, talks to both. Here the mediator is the US, acting through envoys Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner.

steps.title: Shuttle: separate rooms, one messenger
steps.text: Shuttle diplomacy means the mediator meets each side separately and carries offers back and forth. On 12 November the envoys met Putin in Moscow, then Zelensky near Dublin, hours apart.

steps.title: Trilateral: everyone in one room
steps.text: A trilateral round puts all three sides at one table. That happened in Abu Dhabi on 10–11 November, and Witkoff says the format has restarted with a new meeting set.

steps.title: Small wins build trust
steps.text: Sides start with easy, checkable deals, like swapping prisoners. Each promise kept makes the next, harder step, such as territory or security, easier to attempt.

steps.title: Every new seat adds links
steps.text: Every party at the table must agree with every other party. A new seat links to all the seats already there, so the number of pairs that must agree grows fast.

example.setup: Imagine a peace table with three seats: Side A, Side B and a mediator, M. Every pair of seats must reach agreement. Now a fourth party, E, asks to join.

lines.label: Pairs with 3 seats
lines.note: Each pair must be on the same page.

lines.label: Add seat E
lines.calc: E links to A, B and M = 3 new
lines.note: A new seat links to every existing seat.

lines.label: Pairs with 4 seats
lines.note: One extra seat doubled the pairs.

lines.label: Yeses for a deal
lines.note: Any single 'no' blocks the deal.

example.result: Adding one party doubled the pairs that must agree, from 3 to 6, and added a fourth yes. That slows a deal down. If the new party is itself a group, it must agree internally first.

apply.text: Abu Dhabi had three sides: Russia, Ukraine and the US. Zelensky says Europeans will have a team at the next meeting. If it counts as one side, that makes four sides and six pairs. But the team is five countries plus EU diplomats, who must first agree among themselves; Costa says Europe must speak with one clear voice. Peskov says no decision on including Europe has been made.

practice.q: Suppose the four sides become five, with one more party joining. How many pairs must agree now, and how many yeses are needed?
practice.answer: The new seat links to the four seats already there: 4 new pairs. Before, there were 6 pairs. So 6 + 4 = 10 pairs. With five seats, five yeses are needed for a deal.

scenes.say: Toh itna idhar udhar aana jaana kyon? Russia aur Ukraine ek dusre par bharosa nahi karte. Isliye America dono ke beech offers le jaata hai, aur kabhi kabhi dono ko ek kamre mein bitha deta hai. Pehle chhote steps aate hain, jaise prisoner swap, kyunki har side dekh sakti hai ki dusri side ne apna kaam kiya.

scenes.say: Lekin sabse mushkil mudda jaise ka taisa hai. Putin ab bhi Ukraine ki us zameen par control maangte hain, jise Russia annex karne ka daava karta hai. Aur unhone Ukraine mein foreign peacekeeping troops ko saaf mana kar diya hai.

Phir bhi Moscow ko Europe ke liye ek naya security system bhi chahiye. Matlab Europe ki seat ek rukawat bhi hai, aur Russia ki maang bhi.
scenes.speak: फिर आता है Europe। Kushner कहते हैं Europe के बिना कोई deal मुमकिन नहीं। Moscow नहीं चाहता कि Europeans direct talks में हों, क्योंकि वो Ukraine को fund और हथियार देते हैं। फिर भी Moscow को Europe के लिए एक नया security system भी चाहिए। मतलब Europe की seat एक रुकावट भी है, और Russia की माँग भी।

stories.headline: A leftover network flaw knocked Microsoft 365 offline in 74 countries
stories.question: Why did Outlook, Teams and Microsoft 365 go down worldwide for many hours?
stories.dek: Microsoft says a recent network change exposed a flaw left from an earlier network capacity upgrade, and its systems came under heavy load. Much of the world's daily work depends on a few cloud firms.

so_far.text: Microsoft 365 is Microsoft's bundle of online work tools: Outlook email, Teams calls and chat, SharePoint for files, and the Copilot AI assistant. They run in Microsoft's cloud, which means its own data centres and network, not your computer. In early coverage on 13 November 2026, the BBC reported that Microsoft was struggling to fix a global outage it called "connectivity problems". Microsoft first said the issue affected the Americas, then said it could affect any region.

what_happened.text: On 13 November 2026, Microsoft said it had addressed the underlying issue. It called the outage a technical problem "not related to cyber or AI / agents". The cause was a flaw left from an earlier network capacity upgrade. Microsoft said the incident "surfaced following a recent network change" and put elevated load on its infrastructure. "We are deeply sorry for the disruption," it said. Its Friday update reported "broad recovery and stability", while some customers and regions were still being restored. Downdetector counted 74 countries and territories hit. Microsoft promised a full post-incident report.

steps.text: Earlier, Microsoft upgraded its network to add capacity, meaning room for more traffic, but the work left a hidden flaw.
The flaw stayed quiet until a recent network change brought it to the surface.
Once it surfaced, Microsoft's infrastructure came under elevated load, and Microsoft reported connectivity problems with its services.
Affected services included Teams, Exchange Online, Defender XDR, SharePoint Online and Copilot, and Microsoft said any region could be hit.
Addressing the underlying issue did not end it at once; service returned to remaining customers and regions step by step.

history.text:
The story starts on 19 July 2024. A faulty software update from the security firm CrowdStrike crashed about 8.5 million Windows systems and led to roughly 5,078 cancelled flights. It is called the largest IT outage in history. It showed that one bad change, sent to many machines at once, can stop work around the world.

From January 2025, the European Union's Digital Operational Resilience Act began to apply. It sets oversight for critical technology suppliers such as cloud firms. Governments were starting to treat these firms as vital infrastructure.

Then the big clouds themselves failed. On 20 October 2025, an Amazon Web Services outage in its US-EAST-1 region took down thousands of sites and apps, including Snapchat and Reddit. On 29 October 2025, a configuration change in Microsoft's Azure Front Door caused an outage of about eight hours. A configuration change is a change to settings, not to the software itself. It hit Microsoft 365, Xbox, Alaska Airlines and Starbucks.

On 22–23 January 2026, a Microsoft 365 outage lasting nearly 10 hours hit North America. Microsoft blamed reduced capacity during maintenance. Routine work on the network had again been followed by a failure.

The outage reported on 13 November 2026 followed the same pattern, but this time it was global. Downdetector counted 74 countries and territories hit, and Microsoft again traced it to earlier network work.

lesson.concept: Why spare capacity keeps cloud services running
lesson.big_idea: A network works while the traffic trying to use it stays below what it can carry. The gap is a safety margin. When a fault eats that margin, failures can spread to everyone sharing the network.

steps.title: Capacity versus load
steps.text: Capacity is how much traffic a network can carry at once. Load is how much traffic is trying to get through. While load stays below capacity, every request gets served.

steps.title: Spare room is the safety margin
steps.text: Engineers keep a network well below full on purpose. The spare room absorbs sudden spikes or a broken part. Capacity upgrades exist to add more of this room.

steps.title: Changes can quietly shrink capacity
steps.text: A flawed upgrade or maintenance can remove capacity without anyone noticing, until traffic shifts onto it. In January 2026 Microsoft blamed an outage on reduced capacity during maintenance.

steps.title: Overload feeds on itself
steps.text: Once load passes capacity, some requests fail. Apps and people then retry, which adds even more load. So a small shortfall can grow into widespread errors.

steps.title: Many services, one fault
steps.text: When several services depend on the same network, one overload can hit them all. Microsoft has not said how its services share infrastructure, but Teams, Exchange Online, SharePoint and Copilot were all affected.

example.setup: Imagine a cloud email service with 10 network links. Each link carries 100 units of traffic. Normal demand is 700 units.

example.result: Losing 30% of capacity did not cause trouble alone. It erased the safety margin, and retries then pushed demand over the edge, so errors spread to everyone using the network.

apply.text: Microsoft said a flaw left from an earlier capacity upgrade surfaced after a recent network change and put elevated load on its infrastructure. That matches the pattern in our example: a change exposed a weakness, and load rose. Microsoft has given no figures, so how much capacity was lost, and why so many services failed at once, should come from its promised report.

practice.q: Same service, but the faulty change knocks out only two links. Does it still work, and how much spare room is left?
practice.answer: Capacity: 8 × 100 = 800 units. Demand: 700 units. 700 ÷ 800 = 87.5% full. Load stays below capacity, so requests succeed and nobody retries. Spare room: 800 − 700 = 100 units, a thin margin for any spike.

scenes.say: Ab iske peeche ka idea: spare capacity cloud ko chalta kyun rakhti hai. Capacity matlab network kitna traffic utha sakta hai. Load matlab kitna traffic guzarne ki koshish kar raha hai. Jab tak load capacity se neeche hai, sab chalta hai. Yeh gap hi aapka safety margin hai.
scenes.speak: अब इसके पीछे का idea: spare capacity cloud को चलता क्यों रखती है। Capacity मतलब network कितना traffic उठा सकता है। Load मतलब कितना traffic गुज़रने की कोशिश कर रहा है। जब तक load capacity से नीचे है, सब चलता है। यह gap ही आपका safety margin है।

scenes.say: Engineers yeh margin jaan boojh kar rakhte hain, taaki spikes aur toote parts ko jhel sakein. Lekin ek flawed upgrade chupchaap capacity ghata sakta hai. Jaise hi load capacity se aage gaya, requests fail hone lagti hain. Log aur apps retry karte hain, aur load badh jata hai. Aur jab kai services ek hi network par tiki hon, toh ek overload sabko hit kar sakta hai.
scenes.speak: Engineers यह margin जान बूझ कर रखते हैं, ताकि spikes और टूटे parts को झेल सकें। लेकिन एक flawed upgrade चुपचाप capacity घटा सकता है। जैसे ही load capacity से आगे गया, requests fail होने लगती हैं। लोग और apps retry करते हैं, और load बढ़ जाता है। और जब कई services एक ही network पर टिकी हों, तो एक overload सबको hit कर सकता है।

scenes.say: Chaliye ek example lete hain. Maan lijiye ek cloud email service hai, jismein 10 links hain. Har link 100 units traffic le jata hai. Full capacity hui 1000 units. Normal demand hai 700. Yaani 70 percent full, aur 300 units spare.
scenes.speak: चलिए एक example लेते हैं। मान लीजिए एक cloud email service है, जिसमें 10 links हैं। हर link 100 units traffic ले जाता है। Full capacity हुई 1000 units। Normal demand है 700। यानी 70 percent full, और 300 units spare।

scenes.say: Ab maan lijiye ek faulty change 3 links gira deta hai. Capacity gir kar 700 ho gayi, bilkul demand ke barabar. Fail hue users retry karte hain. Maan lijiye isse 20 percent aur jud gaya, toh demand ho gayi 840. 140 units fail. Matlab 6 mein se 1 request fail.
scenes.speak: अब मान लीजिए एक faulty change 3 links गिरा देता है। Capacity गिर कर 700 हो गई, बिल्कुल demand के बराबर। Fail हुए users retry करते हैं। मान लीजिए इससे 20 percent और जुड़ गया, तो demand हो गई 840। 140 units fail। मतलब 6 में से 1 request fail।

scenes.say: India mein aapke liye iska kya matlab hai? Yahan outage ne Microsoft ka cloud email disrupt kiya, jisse business ke kaam aur airline customer support par asar pada. Microsoft ne koi compensation ya service credits announce nahi kiye hain. Ek simple step: urgent kaam ke liye colleagues tak pahunchne ka ek backup tareeka ready rakhiye.
scenes.show: India: offices and airline support hit
scenes.speak: India में आपके लिए इसका क्या मतलब है? यहां outage ने Microsoft का cloud email disrupt किया, जिससे business के काम और airline customer support पर असर पड़ा। Microsoft ने कोई compensation या service credits announce नहीं किए हैं। एक simple step: urgent काम के लिए colleagues तक पहुंचने का एक backup तरीका ready रखिए।

scenes.say: Hamara lesson ismein kaise fit hota hai? Microsoft kehta hai ki ek recent change ne ek purana flaw expose kiya, aur uske systems par load badha. Yahi pattern hamare example mein tha. Lekin Microsoft ne koi figures nahi diye. Kitni capacity gayi, aur itni services ek saath kyun fail huin, yeh uski report se pata chalna chahiye.
scenes.speak: हमारा lesson इसमें कैसे fit होता है? Microsoft कहता है कि एक recent change ने एक पुराना flaw expose किया, और उसके systems पर load बढ़ा। यही pattern हमारे example में था। लेकिन Microsoft ने कोई figures नहीं दिए। कितनी capacity गई, और इतनी services एक साथ क्यों fail हुईं, यह उसकी report से पता चलना चाहिए।

scenes.say: Aage kya? Microsoft ne full post-incident report ka vaada kiya hai, par koi date nahi di. Dekhiye ki exact root cause kya tha aur kitni capacity gayi. Jo ab tak pata nahi: exact start aur end time, kaun si Indian firms aur airlines hit huin, aur customers ko credits milenge ya nahi.
scenes.speak: आगे क्या? Microsoft ने full post-incident report का वादा किया है, पर कोई date नहीं दी। देखिए कि exact root cause क्या था और कितनी capacity गई। जो अब तक पता नहीं: exact start और end time, कौन सी Indian firms और airlines hit हुईं, और customers को credits मिलेंगे या नहीं।

scenes.say: Teen baatein yaad rakhiye. Network tab tak chalta hai jab tak load capacity se neeche hai. Spare room faults ko jhel leta hai. Microsoft ke upgrade ke ek bache hue flaw ne 74 countries aur territories mein Outlook, Teams aur Copilot ko hit kiya. Aur Microsoft ki report, aur kisi bhi service credits par nazar rakhiye.
scenes.show: Spare capacity is the safety margin
scenes.speak: तीन बातें याद रखिए। Network तब तक चलता है जब तक load capacity से नीचे है। Spare room faults को झेल लेता है। Microsoft के upgrade के एक बचे हुए flaw ने 74 countries और territories में Outlook, Teams और Copilot को hit किया। और Microsoft की report, और किसी भी service credits पर नज़र रखिए।

stories.headline: Record exports, yet India's goods trade gap hits a one-year high
stories.question: Why did India's trade deficit widen in the same month its exports hit a record?
stories.dek: Imports rose by more dollars than exports did. Costlier oil and gold bought before Diwali pushed the import bill to $89.35bn. Once services are counted, the gap is much smaller: $20.09bn.

so_far.text: India buys more goods from the world than it sells, but it earns a surplus on services. That means it sells more services abroad than it buys. In September 2026 the goods trade deficit was $30.21bn. The Reserve Bank of India (RBI) said September's current account deficit was $7.4bn, up from $5.2bn a year earlier. That is the broadest measure of what India pays to and earns from the world. From April to October 2026, goods-and-services exports were an estimated $568.84bn, up 16.66%. Exports to the US rose to $59.52bn from $51.99bn. Imports grew 16% too, so the combined deficit for those months widened to $93.35bn from $83.25bn.

what_happened.text: On 13 November 2026, October's trade figures were published. India's goods exports were $49.47bn, which officials called the highest monthly figure ever. Goods imports were $89.35bn. So the goods trade deficit, which is imports minus exports, widened to $39.88bn, a one-year high. In September it was $30.21bn, and a Reuters poll had forecast $32.25bn. Oil imports rose 54.31% from a year earlier to $22.82bn because crude cost more. Gold imports more than tripled from September to $5.51bn as people bought before Diwali.

steps.text: A trade deficit is imports minus exports, so it widens whenever imports rise by more dollars than exports do.
Higher crude prices pushed oil imports up 54.31% from a year earlier, to $22.82bn in October.
Gold bought before Diwali tripled gold imports from September, which explains about $3.7bn of the $9.7bn monthly rise in the deficit.
Imports were about 1.8 times exports, so even record exports could not keep pace in dollars.
Services earned a $19.79bn surplus, which shrank the combined goods-and-services gap to $20.09bn.

history.text: The story starts in August 2025. The US put a 25% tariff, which is a tax on imports, on Indian goods. It added a 25% penalty over India's purchases of Russian oil, so the total duty was 50%. The damage showed in October 2025. India's goods exports fell 11.8% to $34.38bn. Gold imports surged about 200% to $14.7bn, and the goods deficit hit a record $41.68bn. On 6–7 February 2026 the two countries released an interim trade framework. It cut the US tariff on Indian goods to 18%, and the Russian-oil penalty was withdrawn. On 20 February 2026 the US Supreme Court ruled 6-3 that a law called IEEPA does not allow tariffs. A temporary global duty under Section 122 replaced those tariffs, putting India at about 10% for up to 150 days. Reports say that in July 2026 the US added a 10% tariff through a Section 301 action. Commerce Minister Piyush Goyal then said the first part of the deal would take effect only once the US guaranteed India a tariff edge over rival countries. That weak October 2025 is the base that October 2026's export jump is measured against.

lesson.concept: How a trade deficit can widen while exports grow
lesson.big_idea: A trade deficit is the gap between two big numbers: imports and exports. It widens when imports add more dollars than exports do, even if exports are growing fast.

steps.title: The deficit is a gap
steps.text: A trade deficit is imports minus exports. If a country buys $90 of goods from abroad and sells $50, the gap is $40. Both numbers can grow while the gap still changes.

steps.title: Count dollars, not per cent
steps.text: The gap moves by the dollars each side adds, not by percentages. When imports are the bigger number, the same per cent rise adds more dollars to imports than to exports.

steps.title: Prices and seasons swing imports
steps.text: Some imports jump fast. In October 2026 India's oil imports rose 54.31% in a year on higher crude prices. Gold imports tripled from September, before Diwali.

steps.title: Goods are only part
steps.text: Countries also trade services. India's October services surplus of $19.79bn shrank the combined goods-and-services gap to $20.09bn. That is why headlines quote different deficits.

steps.title: The widest measure
steps.text: The current account deficit adds income and transfers, such as money sent home from abroad. The RBI put September 2026's current account deficit at $7.4bn.

example.setup: Imagine a small country that sells ₹100 of goods abroad each month and buys ₹180. Next month, exports and imports both grow by 10%. Assume it also earns ₹40 more from services than it spends.

lines.label: Starting gap
lines.note: Imports minus exports.

lines.label: Imports grow 10%
lines.note: 10% of ₹180 is ₹18, so more rupees.

lines.label: New goods gap
lines.note: Wider by ₹8, though both grew by the same per cent.

lines.label: Add services surplus
lines.note: Services cover part of the goods gap.

example.result: The goods gap widened even though both sides grew by the same per cent, because imports were the bigger number. With services counted, the overall gap was much smaller. That is India's October in miniature.

practice.q: Exports are ₹50 and imports are ₹90. Exports grow 20%, but imports grow only 15%. Does the gap widen or shrink?
practice.answer: Exports: 20% of ₹50 = ₹10, so ₹60. Imports: 15% of ₹90 = ₹13.50, so ₹103.50. New gap: ₹103.50 − ₹60 = ₹43.50, up from ₹40. Exports grew faster in per cent, but the gap still widened.

terms.meaning: How much more a country spends on imports than it earns from exports.
Trade in physical goods like oil, gold and phones, not services.
Earning more from selling services abroad than paying for services from abroad.

scenes.say: Toh deficit chauda kyun hua? Pehli baat, deficit hai imports minus exports. Yeh tab badhta hai jab imports exports se zyada dollar jodte hain. Doosri, mehngi crude ki wajah se oil imports ek saal mein chauvan percent badhe.

scenes.say: Ab ek saal pehle se compare kijiye. Is October ka deficit pichhle October ke record iktaalees point saat billion dollar se kam hai. Exports lagbhag 15 billion zyada hain. The Hindu kehta hai ki isse lagta hai zyada maal bik raha hai, sirf oonchi keemat par nahi.
scenes.speak: अब एक साल पहले से compare कीजिए। इस October का deficit पिछले October के record इकतालीस point सात billion dollar से कम है। Exports लगभग 15 billion ज़्यादा हैं। The Hindu कहता है कि इससे लगता है ज़्यादा माल बिक रहा है, सिर्फ़ ऊँची क़ीमत पर नहीं।

scenes.say: Ab woh baat jisse sab clear hoga. Trade deficit do bade numbers ke beech ka gap hai. Yeh dollar mein chalta hai, percent mein nahi. Jab imports bade hon, toh wahi percent badhat imports mein zyada dollar jodti hai.
scenes.speak: अब वो बात जिससे सब clear होगा। Trade deficit दो बड़े numbers के बीच का gap है। यह dollar में चलता है, percent में नहीं। जब imports बड़े हों, तो वही percent बढ़त imports में ज़्यादा dollar जोड़ती है।

scenes.say: Do aur baatein. Keemat aur season imports ko tezi se hilaate hain: mehnga oil, tyohaar ka gold. Aur goods trade ka sirf ek hissa hain. Services aur transfers, jaise videsh se ghar bheja paisa, goods gap ka bada hissa cover karte hain. Isliye headlines alag alag deficit batati hain.
scenes.speak: दो और बातें। क़ीमत और season imports को तेज़ी से हिलाते हैं: महँगा oil, त्योहार का gold। और goods trade का सिर्फ़ एक हिस्सा हैं। Services और transfers, जैसे विदेश से घर भेजा पैसा, goods gap का बड़ा हिस्सा cover करते हैं। इसलिए headlines अलग अलग deficit बताती हैं।

scenes.say: Chaliye karke dekhte hain. Maan lijiye ek desh 100 rupaye ka maal export karta hai. Import karta hai 180 ka. Gap hua 80. Dono 10 percent badhte hain. Exports mein 10 jude, ho gaye 110. Imports mein 18 jude, ho gaye 198.
scenes.speak: चलिए करके देखते हैं। मान लीजिए एक देश 100 रुपये का माल export करता है। Import करता है 180 का। Gap हुआ 80। दोनों 10 percent बढ़ते हैं। Exports में 10 जुड़े, हो गए 110। Imports में 18 जुड़े, हो गए 198।

scenes.say: Naya gap hai 198 minus 110, yaani 88 rupaye. Dono barabar badhe, phir bhi gap chauda! Ab maan lijiye 40 rupaye ka services surplus hai. Overall gap gir kar 48 ho jaata hai. Yahi hai India ka October, chhote roop mein.
scenes.speak: नया gap है 198 minus 110, यानी 88 रुपये। दोनों बराबर बढ़े, फिर भी gap चौड़ा! अब मान लीजिए 40 रुपये का services surplus है। Overall gap गिर कर 48 हो जाता है। यही है India का October, छोटे रूप में।

scenes.say: Aapke liye iska matlab kya? Agar aapne Diwali se pehle gold khareeda, toh aap is number ka hissa hain. Mehngi crude ne India ka oil bill badhaya. Electronics, gems aur jewellery, aur baaki goods ne export growth chalayi. Aur yaad rakhiye: bada deficit matlab kamzor exports nahi. Yahan exports record par the.
scenes.speak: आपके लिए इसका मतलब क्या? अगर आपने Diwali से पहले gold ख़रीदा, तो आप इस number का हिस्सा हैं। महँगी crude ने India का oil bill बढ़ाया। Electronics, gems और jewellery, और बाक़ी goods ने export growth चलाई। और याद रखिए: बड़ा deficit मतलब कमज़ोर exports नहीं। यहाँ exports record पर थे।

scenes.say: Ab yeh sabak lagaiye. India ke imports uske exports ke lagbhag ek point aath guna the. Toh oil aur gold ne record exports se zyada dollar jode, aur goods gap chauda hua. Phir unnees point aath billion dollar ke services surplus ne combined gap ko lagbhag 20 billion par la diya.
scenes.speak: अब यह सबक लगाइए। India के imports उसके exports के लगभग एक point आठ गुना थे। तो oil और gold ने record exports से ज़्यादा dollar जोड़े, और goods gap चौड़ा हुआ। फिर उन्नीस point आठ billion dollar के services surplus ने combined gap को लगभग 20 billion पर ला दिया।

scenes.say: Aage kya? December 2026 mein India US talks ka ek aur round plan hai. India US ki Section 301 probes ka intezaar kar raha hai, jo tariffs badha sakti hain. Bloomberg, ek anaam official ke hawale se, kehta hai US ne India ko rivals se kam tariff ka vaada kiya. US ne on record iski pushti nahi ki. Aur oil par nazar rakhiye: Brent lagbhag 95 dollar per barrel hai.
scenes.speak: आगे क्या? December 2026 में India US talks का एक और round plan है। India US की Section 301 probes का इंतज़ार कर रहा है, जो tariffs बढ़ा सकती हैं। Bloomberg, एक अनाम official के हवाले से, कहता है US ने India को rivals से कम tariff का वादा किया। US ने on record इसकी पुष्टि नहीं की। और oil पर नज़र रखिए: Brent लगभग 95 dollar per barrel है।

scenes.say: Teen baatein yaad rakhiye. Trade deficit ek gap hai, aur yeh tab badhta hai jab imports exports se zyada dollar jodte hain. October 2026 mein mehnga oil aur Diwali gold record exports se aage nikal gaye. Aur December ki trade talks, Section 301 probes aur oil prices par nazar rakhiye.
scenes.speak: तीन बातें याद रखिए। Trade deficit एक gap है, और यह तब बढ़ता है जब imports exports से ज़्यादा dollar जोड़ते हैं। October 2026 में महँगा oil और Diwali gold record exports से आगे निकल गए। और December की trade talks, Section 301 probes और oil prices पर नज़र रखिए।

stories.headline: Minibus-truck crash near Kaziranga kills 24, many of them students
stories.question: How did 24 people, including students, die in a bus-truck crash near Kaziranga?
stories.dek: Police say a minibus carrying college students was likely speeding when the driver lost control and hit a container truck head-on. The stretch has low speed limits because it runs beside Kaziranga.

so_far.text: NH-715 runs along the southern edge of Kaziranga National Park in Golaghat district, Assam. Animals cross it, and a study found vehicle speed was the main factor in roadkill there. So seasonal speed limits of about 40 kmph and fines apply. People have died on this road too. In January 2024 a head-on bus-truck collision near Dergaon killed about 12 people. In October 2025 the Union Cabinet approved widening the road to four lanes.

what_happened.text: On 13 November 2026 a minibus and a container truck collided head-on at Rangajan, near Hathikuli Tea Estate, on NH-715 in Golaghat district. The minibus was going from Golaghat to Nagaon. At least 24 people died. Many were college students returning from classes. The dead include two women, a minor, the minibus driver and a handyman. About 20 were injured and referred to Jorhat. Early reports gave 23 dead and varying injury counts. Police said the driver likely lost control while speeding.

steps.text: NH-715 runs beside Kaziranga, so the stretch has low seasonal speed limits of about 40 kmph.
Police say the minibus was running at high speed, breaking those limits, and the driver likely lost control.
A vehicle out of control can drift into the oncoming lane, which is how a head-on crash happens.
In a head-on crash the two speeds add up, and crash energy grows with the square of speed.
A minibus is far lighter than a container truck, so the people inside it take the harsher jolt.

history.text:
The story begins with a park. Lady Curzon visited Kaziranga in 1904, and that visit led to protection for its rhinos. In 1905 a 232 sq km reserve forest was created. It became a national park on 11 February 1974 and a UNESCO World Heritage Site in 1985. Each step raised the level of protection.

A highway, once called NH-37 and now NH-715, skirts the park's southern boundary. That put fast traffic where animals cross. Animal corridors were set up across it. The 2005 documentary Jaws of Death showed animals killed by vehicles on it. A 2016–17 study reportedly counted 6,036 roadkill incidents on the stretch, 63.6% during floods, with vehicle speed the main factor. Seasonal limits of about 40 kmph and fines now apply.

People have died on this road too. On 3 January 2024 a head-on bus-truck crash near Dergaon, Golaghat, killed about 12. An official linked it to a damaged part of the highway, fog and speeding.

On 1 October 2025 the Union Cabinet approved four lanes for about 86 km, from Kaliabor to Numaligarh, at ₹6,957 crore. The plan includes a roughly 34.5 km elevated corridor through Kaziranga for wildlife. Groundbreaking was reported in January 2026, with completion expected around 2029.

lesson.concept: Why speed makes a crash far deadlier
lesson.big_idea: A moving vehicle carries energy that must go somewhere in a crash. That energy grows with the square of speed, so twice as fast means four times the energy and a much longer stop.

steps.title: Moving things carry energy
steps.text: Any moving vehicle carries kinetic energy, the energy of motion. To stop safely, brakes turn it into heat. In a crash, metal and human bodies absorb it instead.

steps.title: Energy grows with speed squared
steps.text: Kinetic energy depends on speed multiplied by itself. Double the speed and the energy becomes four times. Triple it and the energy becomes nine times.

steps.title: Stopping takes far longer
steps.text: Braking distance, how far a vehicle travels once brakes are applied, also grows with the square of speed. The distance covered while the driver reacts grows in step with speed.

steps.title: Head-on crashes combine speeds
steps.text: When two vehicles meet head-on, their speeds add up. The lighter vehicle, like a minibus against a container truck, gets the harsher jolt.

steps.title: Why Kaziranga's limit is low
steps.text: On NH-715 near Kaziranga, seasonal limits of about 40 kmph and fines apply. A study found speed was the main factor in animal deaths there. Low speed shrinks both energy and stopping distance.

example.setup: Imagine the same minibus on the same road, once at 40 kmph and once at 80 kmph. Assume it needs 10 metres to brake to a stop at 40 kmph.

lines.label: Speed ratio
lines.note: Twice as fast.

lines.label: Energy at 40
lines.note: Energy follows speed times speed.

lines.label: Energy at 80
lines.note: Same rule, higher speed.

lines.label: Energy compared
lines.note: Doubling speed quadruples the energy.

lines.label: Braking distance
lines.note: Braking distance grows the same way, before reaction time.

example.result: Doubling speed does not double the danger. It gives a crash four times the energy and needs four times the braking distance, so a driver has far less room to recover.

practice.q: A truck runs at 120 kmph on a stretch with a 40 kmph limit. How many times more crash energy does it carry?
practice.answer: Speed ratio: 120 ÷ 40 = 3. Energy grows with the square: 3 × 3 = 9. So it carries nine times the energy. If it brakes in 10 metres at 40 kmph, it needs about 90 metres at 120.

stories.headline: India cuts TB deaths faster than the world, but cases stay high
stories.question: Is India winning against TB, given that it still has a quarter of the world's cases?
stories.dek: Partly. WHO says India's TB deaths fell 38% between 2015 and 2025, faster than the world's 35%. But India still reported 25.3 lakh cases in 2025, the year it hoped to end TB.

so_far.text: Tuberculosis (TB) is a bacterial disease that mostly attacks the lungs. It can be cured with months of medicine. In 2015 the world adopted the End TB Strategy. It set targets measured against 2015 levels: 75% fewer deaths and 50% fewer new cases by 2025, then 90% and 80% by 2030. In 2020 India's government set a goal of ending TB by 2025, five years ahead of the global 2030 target. Each year the World Health Organization (WHO) tracks every country in its Global TB Report.

what_happened.text: On 12 November 2026 WHO released its Global TB Report 2026. It says India's estimated TB deaths fell 38% from 2015 to 2025, against 35% worldwide. India's TB death rate fell from 28 to 18 per lakh people. India reported 25.3 lakh cases and 2.63 lakh deaths in 2025, down from 26.18 lakh cases and just over 3 lakh deaths in 2024. It still has about a quarter of world cases, the most of any country. WHO left out India's estimate of new cases pending review. Worldwide, the 2025 milestones were missed.

steps.text: Finding TB early matters: an untreated person keeps spreading the disease and gets sicker.
From December 2024, the TB Mukt Bharat campaign screened over 25 crore people and found 48.64 lakh cases.
Programmes credited for the progress include Ni-kshay digital tracking and Ni-kshay Poshan Yojana nutrition support; India's treatment success is 94%.
These likely helped the death rate fall from 28 to 18 per lakh, though the campaign began only near the end of 2015–2025.
New cases fall more slowly, about 21% from 2015 to 2024, so India still holds about a quarter of world cases.

history.text: India has fought TB for more than a century. Its first national TB study came in 1914, and the Tuberculosis Association of India followed in 1939. The big shift came in 1997, when India launched the Revised National TB Control Programme (RNTCP). It used WHO's DOTS method, where a health worker watches patients take their medicine. The aim was treatment success for at least 85% of new patients. In 2010 the programme adopted universal access: quality diagnosis and treatment for all TB patients. In 2015 the world set the End TB targets, measured against 2015 levels. By 2018 India was notifying 21.5 lakh new TB patients a year. On 30 December 2019 the RNTCP was renamed the National TB Elimination Programme (NTEP). The aim moved from controlling TB to ending it. In 2020 the government set 2025 as its deadline. On 7 December 2024 India began the TB Mukt Bharat Abhiyaan, a mass campaign to find hidden cases. Then money became a worry. In November 2025 WHO warned that if cuts to USAID and Global Fund money were not replaced, there could be about 2 million extra TB deaths from 2025 to 2035.

lesson.concept: How rates and shares measure progress against disease
lesson.big_idea: A count tells you how many people are ill. A rate per lakh tells you how common it is. A share tells you your slice of the world's total. Each answers a different question.

steps.title: Start with the count
steps.text: A count is the plain total: how many people fell ill or died in a year. India reported 25.3 lakh TB cases in 2025. But a count alone hides how big the population is.

steps.title: Turn it into a rate
steps.text: Divide the count by the population, then multiply by 1,00,000. That gives a rate per lakh, so big and small places compare fairly. India's TB death rate was 18 per lakh in 2025.

steps.title: Compare with a starting year
steps.text: Progress is the percentage change from a base year: (old − new) ÷ old × 100. The End TB targets use 2015 as the base: 75% fewer deaths by 2025, 90% by 2030.

steps.title: A share is a slice
steps.text: Share = your count ÷ world count × 100. It depends on your size and on how fast others improve. So a big country can cut its rate and still hold a large share. India's is about a quarter.

example.setup: Imagine a district of 10 lakh people. In 2015, 300 people there died of TB. In 2025 the population is still 10 lakh, and 180 people die of TB.

example.result: The district cut its death rate by 40%, which is real progress. Yet it is far from the 75% milestone and still holds a big share. Whether it is 'winning' depends on which measure you ask about.

apply.text: India's TB death rate fell from 28 to 18 per lakh between 2015 and 2025, and WHO says deaths fell 38%, beating the world's 35%. That is real progress on the rate. But the 2025 milestone was a 75% cut, and India still holds about a quarter of world cases. Both are true at once.

practice.q: A city of 20 lakh people had 400 TB deaths in 2015 and 200 in 2025, with the same population. What was the fall, and did it meet the 75% milestone?
practice.answer: 2015 rate: 400 ÷ 20 lakh × 1 lakh = 20 per lakh. 2025 rate: 200 ÷ 20 lakh × 1 lakh = 10 per lakh. Fall: (20 − 10) ÷ 20 × 100 = 50%. The milestone needed 75%, a rate of 5 per lakh. So it fell short.

check.why: A rate and a share answer different questions. A big country can cut its rate and still hold a large slice of world cases.

takeaways: A rate per lakh shows how common a disease is; a share shows your slice of the world.

scenes.speak: दुनिया के लगभग एक चौथाई TB cases India में हैं, किसी भी और देश से ज़्यादा। फिर भी India में TB से मौतें दुनिया से तेज़ गिर रही हैं। तो क्या India TB से जीत रहा है? कुछ हद तक। चलिए समझते हैं क्यों।

scenes.say: 12 November 2026 ko World Health Organization, yaani WHO, ne apni Global TB Report jaari ki. Isme likha hai ki 2015 se 2025 ke beech India mein TB se andaazan mautein 38 percent giri. Poori duniya mein yeh girawat 35 percent thi.
scenes.speak: 12 November 2026 को World Health Organization, यानी WHO, ने अपनी Global TB Report जारी की। इसमें लिखा है कि 2015 से 2025 के बीच India में TB से अंदाज़न मौतें 38 percent गिरीं। पूरी दुनिया में यह गिरावट 35 percent थी।

scenes.say: 2025 mein India ne pachchis point teen lakh TB cases aur do point chhe teen lakh mautein report ki. 2024 mein chhabbis point ek aath lakh cases the, aur teen lakh se thodi zyada mautein. WHO ne India ke naye cases ka estimate report mein shaamil nahi kiya, kyunki review pending hai. Aur duniya apne 2025 ke milestones se chook gayi.
scenes.speak: 2025 में India ने पच्चीस point तीन लाख TB cases और दो point छह तीन लाख मौतें report कीं। 2024 में छब्बीस point एक आठ लाख cases थे, और तीन लाख से थोड़ी ज़्यादा मौतें। WHO ने India के नए cases का estimate report में शामिल नहीं किया, क्योंकि review pending है। और दुनिया अपने 2025 के milestones से चूक गई।

scenes.say: Yahan tak pahunche kaise? India ki pehli national TB study 1914 mein aayi. 1939 mein Tuberculosis Association of India bana. Bada badlaav 1997 mein aaya, Revised National TB Control Programme ke saath. Isme WHO ka DOTS method use hua, jisme ek health worker apne saamne mareez ko dawai khilata hai. Target tha 85 percent treatment success.
scenes.show: 1997: DOTS, a health worker watches each dose
scenes.speak: यहाँ तक पहुँचे कैसे? India की पहली national TB study 1914 में आई। 1939 में Tuberculosis Association of India बना। बड़ा बदलाव 1997 में आया, Revised National TB Control Programme के साथ। इसमें WHO का DOTS method use हुआ, जिसमें एक health worker अपने सामने मरीज़ को दवाई खिलाता है। Target था 85 percent treatment success।

scenes.say: 2010 mein programme ne sabhi patients ke liye achhi quality diagnosis aur treatment ka vaada kiya. 2015 mein duniya ne apne End TB targets tay kiye. 2018 tak India har saal ikkis point paanch lakh naye patients notify kar raha tha. December 2019 mein programme ka naam bana National TB Elimination Programme. Aur 2020 mein India ne TB khatam karne ki deadline 2025 rakhi.
scenes.show: From controlling TB to ending it
scenes.speak: 2010 में programme ने सभी patients के लिए अच्छी quality diagnosis और treatment का वादा किया। 2015 में दुनिया ने अपने End TB targets तय किए। 2018 तक India हर साल इक्कीस point पाँच लाख नए patients notify कर रहा था। December 2019 में programme का नाम बना National TB Elimination Programme। और 2020 में India ने TB ख़त्म करने की deadline 2025 रखी।

timeline.what: First national TB study
RNTCP launched with DOTS
Universal access to diagnosis and treatment
End TB targets set
Renamed National TB Elimination Programme
Goal: end TB by 2025
TB Mukt Bharat campaign begins
WHO: India TB deaths down 38%

scenes.say: December 2024 mein India ne TB Mukt Bharat Abhiyaan shuru kiya, chhupe hue cases dhoondhne ki ek badi muhim. Phir November 2025 mein WHO ne chetavani di: agar American aid aur Global Fund mein hui katauti ki bharpaai nahi hui, toh 2025 se 2035 ke beech lagbhag 2 million extra mautein ho sakti hain.
scenes.image: United States Agency for International Development
scenes.speak: December 2024 में India ने TB Mukt Bharat Abhiyaan शुरू किया, छुपे हुए cases ढूँढने की एक बड़ी मुहिम। फिर November 2025 में WHO ने चेतावनी दी: अगर American aid और Global Fund में हुई कटौती की भरपाई नहीं हुई, तो 2025 से 2035 के बीच लगभग 2 million extra मौतें हो सकती हैं।

scenes.say: Yahi End TB targets paimaana hain. 2015 ke muqable, duniya ka target tha ki 2025 tak mautein 75 percent kam hon aur naye cases 50 percent kam. 2030 tak: 90 aur 80 percent kam. India ne duniya se 5 saal pehle TB khatam karne ka target rakha.
scenes.speak: यही End TB targets पैमाना हैं। 2015 के मुक़ाबले, दुनिया का target था कि 2025 तक मौतें 75 percent कम हों और नए cases 50 percent कम। 2030 तक: 90 और 80 percent कम। India ने दुनिया से 5 साल पहले TB ख़त्म करने का target रखा।

scenes.say: Toh mautein giri kyun? Kai programmes ko iska credit diya jaata hai, lekin aankde yeh nahi batate ki kisne kitni madad ki. Pehla step: TB jaldi pakdo, kyunki bina ilaaj wala mareez TB failata rehta hai aur zyada beemar hota jaata hai. December 2024 se India ki campaign ne 25 crore se zyada logon ki screening ki aur adtalis point chhe chaar lakh cases dhoondhe.
scenes.speak: तो मौतें गिरीं क्यों? कई programmes को इसका credit दिया जाता है, लेकिन आँकड़े यह नहीं बताते कि किसने कितनी मदद की। पहला step: TB जल्दी पकड़ो, क्योंकि बिना इलाज वाला मरीज़ TB फैलाता रहता है और ज़्यादा बीमार होता जाता है। December 2024 से India की campaign ने 25 करोड़ से ज़्यादा लोगों की screening की और अड़तालीस point छह चार लाख cases ढूँढे।

scenes.say: Doosra step: patients ko treatment par tikaaye rakhna. Credit paane wale programmes mein Ni-kshay digital tracking aur Ni-kshay Poshan Yojana ka nutrition support shaamil hain. Teesra step: zyada cure ka matlab shayad kam mautein. Lekin campaign us das saal ke period ke aakhir mein hi shuru hui. Chautha step: naye cases dheere gire, 2015 se 2024 tak lagbhag 21 percent.
scenes.speak: दूसरा step: patients को treatment पर टिकाए रखना। Credit पाने वाले programmes में Ni-kshay digital tracking और Ni-kshay Poshan Yojana का nutrition support शामिल हैं। तीसरा step: ज़्यादा cure का मतलब शायद कम मौतें। लेकिन campaign उस दस साल के period के आख़िर में ही शुरू हुई। चौथा step: नए cases धीरे गिरे, 2015 से 2024 तक लगभग 21 percent।

scenes.say: Ek paani ki tanki sochiye. Naye cases ek tap se andar aate hain. Cure aur mautein drain se bahar jaate hain. India ne drain ko safe banaya: zyada log theek hokar nikle, kam ki maut hui. Lekin tap ab bhi chal raha hai, isliye tanki bhari rehti hai. Yeh misaal kahan tootti hai? Paani failta nahi, lekin TB ke mareez doosron ko infect kar sakte hain.
scenes.show: Safer drain, but the tap still runs
scenes.speak: एक पानी की टंकी सोचिए। नए cases एक tap से अंदर आते हैं। Cure और मौतें drain से बाहर जाते हैं। India ने drain को safe बनाया: ज़्यादा लोग ठीक होकर निकले, कम की मौत हुई। लेकिन tap अब भी चल रहा है, इसलिए टंकी भरी रहती है। यह मिसाल कहाँ टूटती है? पानी फैलता नहीं, लेकिन TB के मरीज़ दूसरों को infect कर सकते हैं।

scenes.say: Ab players ki baat. WHO har saal report card jaari karta hai. Desh ke andar India ka National TB Elimination Programme yeh ladaai chalata hai. USAID, yaani American aid agency, ne 2024 mein TB ke liye 406 million dollar commit kiye. Aur Global Fund ke 2024 se 2026 wale cycle mein ek point chaar billion dollar ki katauti hui.
scenes.speak: अब players की बात। WHO हर साल report card जारी करता है। देश के अंदर India का National TB Elimination Programme यह लड़ाई चलाता है। USAID, यानी American aid agency, ने 2024 में TB के लिए 406 million dollar commit किए। और Global Fund के 2024 से 2026 वाले cycle में एक point चार billion dollar की कटौती हुई।

players.name: USAID
players.role: US aid agency; $406 million to TB, 2024

scenes.say: Sabse saaf number yeh hai. 2015 mein India mein har ek lakh mein se 28 log TB se mare. 2025 tak yeh 18 reh gaya. Matlab har ek lakh logon par 10 mautein kam.
scenes.speak: सबसे साफ़ number यह है। 2015 में India में हर एक लाख में से 28 लोग TB से मरे। 2025 तक यह 18 रह गया। मतलब हर एक लाख लोगों पर 10 मौतें कम।

scenes.say: Cure ke maamle mein India achha kar raha hai: regular TB mein 94 percent success, jabki duniya mein 90 percent. Kamzor kadi hai drug-resistant TB. Duniya bhar mein lagbhag teen point saat lakh naye cases aaye, aur sirf 42 percent ka ilaaj hua.
scenes.speak: Cure के मामले में India अच्छा कर रहा है: regular TB में 94 percent success, जबकि दुनिया में 90 percent। कमज़ोर कड़ी है drug-resistant TB। दुनिया भर में लगभग तीन point सात लाख नए cases आए, और सिर्फ़ 42 percent का इलाज हुआ।

scenes.say: Ab woh idea jo yeh sab suljhata hai. Count batata hai kitne. Rate per lakh batata hai kitna common hai. Share batata hai duniya ke total mein aapka hissa kitna hai. Har ek alag sawaal ka jawab deta hai.
scenes.speak: अब वो idea जो यह सब सुलझाता है। Count बताता है कितने। Rate per lakh बताता है कितना common है। Share बताता है दुनिया के total में आपका हिस्सा कितना है। हर एक अलग सवाल का जवाब देता है।

scenes.say: Pehla step, count: India ke pachchis point teen lakh cases. Lekin count yeh chhupa leta hai ki population kitni badi hai. Doosra step, rate: count ko population se divide kijiye, phir ek lakh se multiply. Ab bade aur chhote ilaake barabari se compare hote hain.
scenes.speak: पहला step, count: India के पच्चीस point तीन लाख cases। लेकिन count यह छुपा लेता है कि population कितनी बड़ी है। दूसरा step, rate: count को population से divide कीजिए, फिर एक लाख से multiply। अब बड़े और छोटे इलाक़े बराबरी से compare होते हैं।

scenes.say: Teesra step, change: purana minus naya, purane se divide, phir sau se multiply, kisi base year jaise 2015 se. Chautha step, share: aapka count divided by duniya ka count. Agar aap bade hain toh yeh bada hi rehta hai, chahe aapka apna rate gir raha ho.
scenes.speak: तीसरा step, change: पुराना minus नया, पुराने से divide, फिर सौ से multiply, किसी base year जैसे 2015 से। चौथा step, share: आपका count divided by दुनिया का count। अगर आप बड़े हैं तो यह बड़ा ही रहता है, चाहे आपका अपना rate गिर रहा हो।

scenes.say: Chaliye karke dekhte hain. Maan lijiye ek district hai, 10 lakh logon ka. 2015 mein 300 log TB se marte hain. Yeh hua 30 per lakh. 2025 mein, population wahi, 180 log marte hain. Ab yeh 18 per lakh hai.
scenes.speak: चलिए करके देखते हैं। मान लीजिए एक district है, 10 लाख लोगों का। 2015 में 300 लोग TB से मरते हैं। यह हुआ 30 per lakh। 2025 में, population वही, 180 लोग मरते हैं। अब यह 18 per lakh है।

scenes.say: Ab girawat. 30 minus 18 hua 12, aur 30 mein se 12 matlab 40 percent. Asli progress. Lekin 75 percent cut ke liye rate saadhe saat chahiye tha. Aur agar state mein 600 mautein hui thi, toh yeh district ab bhi unka 30 percent hai.
scenes.speak: अब गिरावट। 30 minus 18 हुआ 12, और 30 में से 12 मतलब 40 percent। असली progress। लेकिन 75 percent cut के लिए rate साढ़े सात चाहिए था। और अगर state में 600 मौतें हुई थीं, तो यह district अब भी उनका 30 percent है।

scenes.say: Wapas India par. Iska death rate 28 se girkar 18 per lakh hua, duniya se tez. Lekin milestone 75 percent cut ka tha, aur iska share ab bhi ek chauthai hai. Toh ek aam galti hai yeh sochna ki bada share hai toh koi progress nahi. Dono baatein ek saath sach hain.
scenes.speak: वापस India पर। इसका death rate 28 से गिरकर 18 per lakh हुआ, दुनिया से तेज़। लेकिन milestone 75 percent cut का था, और इसका share अब भी एक चौथाई है। तो एक आम ग़लती है यह सोचना कि बड़ा share है तो कोई progress नहीं। दोनों बातें एक साथ सच हैं।

scenes.say: Aapke liye: campaign ko lagbhag 15 lakh aise log mile jinhe TB tha par koi symptom nahi tha, isliye khaansi nahi hai toh TB nahi hai, aisa mat maaniye. Centre ke mutabik India ke TB programme ka lagbhag 96 percent paisa India ke apne resources se aata hai. Aur 2025 mein 67933 panchayaton ko TB-free declare kiya gaya.
scenes.show: 96% of TB funding is India's own
scenes.speak: आपके लिए: campaign को लगभग 15 लाख ऐसे लोग मिले जिन्हें TB था पर कोई symptom नहीं था, इसलिए खाँसी नहीं है तो TB नहीं है, ऐसा मत मानिए। Centre के मुताबिक़ India के TB programme का लगभग 96 percent पैसा India के अपने resources से आता है। और 2025 में 67933 पंचायतों को TB-free declare किया गया।

scenes.say: Aage kya? WHO ko ummeed hai ki India ke naye cases ka updated estimate 2027 ki shuruaat mein aayega. Isse pata chalega ki India TB khatam karne se kitna door hai. Duniya ki agli deadline 2030 hai. Jo ab tak saaf nahi: India ke drug-resistant TB ke numbers, uske national survey ke results, aur 2025 ki aid katauti kitni badi thi.
scenes.speak: आगे क्या? WHO को उम्मीद है कि India के नए cases का updated estimate 2027 की शुरुआत में आएगा। इससे पता चलेगा कि India TB ख़त्म करने से कितना दूर है। दुनिया की अगली deadline 2030 है। जो अब तक साफ़ नहीं: India के drug-resistant TB के numbers, उसके national survey के results, और 2025 की aid कटौती कितनी बड़ी थी।

scenes.say: Teen baatein yaad rakhiye. Rate batata hai bimari kitni common hai, share batata hai duniya mein aapka hissa. 2015 se India mein TB mautein 38 percent giri, duniya se tez, lekin cases ab bhi sabse zyada yahin hain. Aur 2027 ki shuruaat mein WHO ka India estimate dekhte rahiye.
scenes.speak: तीन बातें याद रखिए। Rate बताता है बीमारी कितनी common है, share बताता है दुनिया में आपका हिस्सा। 2015 से India में TB मौतें 38 percent गिरीं, दुनिया से तेज़, लेकिन cases अब भी सबसे ज़्यादा यहीं हैं। और 2027 की शुरुआत में WHO का India estimate देखते रहिए।

thread.previously: The government plans a three-day special Parliament session (no dates yet) to pass the Delimitation Bill. The 131st Amendment failed 298-230 on 17 April 2026, and the bill was marked infructuous. The package raises the Lok Sabha ceiling from 550 to 850. Amit Shah reportedly claims a 15-18 vote margin; Congress calls it bluster. Southern states fear losing their share of seats.
thread.changed: New on 13 November 2026: reports say the Centre is weighing a special session to pass the 33% women's quota with delimitation and an 850-seat Lok Sabha, seeking 361 votes. Dates are still not announced.

stories.headline: Government eyes 361 votes for women's quota in special session
stories.question: Can the government find 361 votes to pass the women's reservation amendment in a special session?
stories.dek: In April the amendment won 298 votes and still failed, short of the 352 two-thirds needed. Reports now put the target at 361. The fight is over tying the women's quota to redrawing seats.

so_far.text: In September 2023 Parliament passed a women's quota law. The quota starts only after a new census and delimitation, and the 2021 Census was postponed indefinitely. On 16 April 2026 the government notified the law, but the quota stays inoperative. On 17 April a linked amendment, which would have enlarged the Lok Sabha to up to 850 seats, failed 298 to 230. The government then withdrew the Delimitation Bill.

what_happened.text: On 13 November 2026, The Financial Express reported that the Centre is weighing a special Parliament session. Its aim is to pass women's reservation and delimitation measures together. These include a 33% quota for women and a Lok Sabha of 850 seats, up from the current 543. The same day, Organiser reported that the government is seeking 361 votes for the constitutional amendment. No session dates have been announced. In April a similar amendment drew 298 votes.

steps.text: A constitutional amendment needs two-thirds of MPs present and voting, not just more yes votes than no votes.
The 2023 women's quota starts only after a new census and delimitation, so it still sits on paper.
The government tied the quota to delimitation and a bigger Lok Sabha; opposition parties back the quota but reject that link.
In April that amendment won 298 votes, more than the 230 against, but below the 352 needed.
So a 361-vote target means winning more yes votes than April's 298, or fewer MPs voting no.

history.text:
The demand is older than the Republic. In 1946, members of the Constituent Assembly asked for seats reserved for women in legislatures, but none was adopted. Fifty years later, in 1996, the Deve Gowda government introduced the first women's reservation bill, the 81st Amendment. Versions in 1998 and 1999 also failed to pass.

A second thread began in 2001. The 84th Amendment froze how seats are allocated among states on the 1971 Census, until the first census after 2026. So states' seat shares stopped following population changes. This freeze is the basis of southern states' concerns about delimitation.

In 2010 the Rajya Sabha passed the 108th Amendment for a women's quota. The Lok Sabha never approved it, and it lapsed in 2014. In September 2023 the quota finally became law as the Nari Shakti Vandan Adhiniyam: 454 to 2 in the Lok Sabha and 214 to 0 in the Rajya Sabha. The President assented on 28 September 2023.

But Article 334A tied the two threads together. The quota starts only after delimitation based on the first census published after the Act, and the 2021 Census was postponed indefinitely. On 16 April 2026 the government notified the Act, yet the quota stays inoperative. On 17 April the 131st Amendment, which would have enlarged the Lok Sabha to up to 850 seats, failed 298 to 230.

analogy.text: Think of a housing society changing its bylaws, which needs two-thirds of members who vote. The committee puts two changes in one resolution: reserve a third of committee posts for women, and redraw how many votes each wing gets. Most members like the first. Some fear the second, and enough no votes sink both.
analogy.breaks: Parliament has two Houses voting separately, and redrawing seats changes how much say whole states get, not single flat owners.

items.view: Wants the 33% women's quota passed together with delimitation measures and an 850-seat Lok Sabha, in a special session.
Support women's reservation but oppose tying it to delimitation, which would enlarge the Lok Sabha up to 850 seats.

for_you.text: If you are a woman hoping to contest a Lok Sabha seat, the 33% quota is law but not yet usable: it waits on a census and delimitation. Delimitation will also decide how many MPs your state sends; seat allocation still rests on the 1971 Census. There is no direct effect on prices or EMIs.

misconception.myth: The women's quota is already in force, so a third of MPs will soon be women.
misconception.fact: The 2023 Act was notified on 16 April 2026, but the 33% quota stays inoperative until a census and delimitation are completed.

lesson.concept: How Parliament passes a constitutional amendment
lesson.big_idea: Changing the Constitution needs more than a simple win. In each House, at least two-thirds of MPs present and voting must say yes, so more than one-third voting no can block it.

steps.title: Ordinary laws need a simple majority
steps.text: Most bills pass if more MPs vote yes than no. If 300 say yes and 200 say no, the bill passes. MPs who are absent or abstain are not counted.

steps.title: Amendments need a special majority
steps.text: Changing the Constitution's text needs two tests in each House. At least two-thirds of MPs present and voting must say yes. And the yes votes must be more than half of the House's total membership.

steps.title: More than one-third can block
steps.text: Flip it around: if more than one-third of those voting say no, the amendment fails. In April 2026, 230 of the 528 MPs voting said no, which is more than one-third.

example.result: Winning 300 to 180 would pass an ordinary bill easily. For an amendment it fails, because yes falls short of two-thirds and the 180 no votes are more than a third.

apply.text: In April 2026 the same arithmetic sank the 131st Amendment. Yes beat no, 298 to 230, but two-thirds of 528 voting was 352. Reports now put the target at 361, so the government needs more yes votes than in April, fewer MPs voting no, or both. Opposition parties back the quota but oppose the delimitation link.

practice.q: Same House of 500 members. This time 30 opponents walk out instead of voting no. So 450 vote: 300 yes, 150 no. Does the amendment pass?
practice.answer: Two-thirds of 450 = 300, and yes votes are 300, so the target is met. Half of 500 is 250; 300 clears it. One-third of 450 is 150, and no votes are exactly 150, not more. It passes: the walkout lowered the target.

stories.headline: Nonprofits sue five AI firms to halt more powerful AI
stories.question: Can a lawsuit really force OpenAI, Google and Anthropic to stop building frontier AI?
stories.dek: Only if a judge agrees, and that would be a first. Four nonprofits want a California court to freeze AI beyond firms' most advanced models as of 12 November 2026, until they prove control.

so_far.text: Frontier AI means the most capable AI models. Since 2023, worried campaigners have tried open letters, summits and laws to slow it. Public Citizen and the Alliance for Secure AI urged the US Congress to strengthen federal AI oversight, arguing self-regulation cannot work. President Trump opposes slowing AI. On 10 November 2026, two days before this lawsuit, Australia announced plans for mandatory frontier AI safety rules.

what_happened.text: On 12 November 2026, four nonprofits sued Anthropic, Google, Meta, OpenAI and SpaceX's AI unit, SpaceX Super Intelligence, in San Francisco Superior Court. The plaintiffs are the Irreplaceable Education Fund, Public Citizen, the Heat Initiative and the Alliance for Secure AI. They bring one claim under California's Unfair Competition Law, saying the firms create a public nuisance that endangers health, safety and property. They ask for an immediate order barring AI more capable than each firm's current best model, and AI that directs AI research on its own. Meta declined to comment; the others did not immediately respond.

steps.text: Campaigners say self-regulation cannot work, and the 2023 call for a six-month pause did not produce any pause.
President Trump opposes slowing AI, saying "whoever wins AI wins". The suit follows Democratic gains in the US midterm elections.
The groups filed in a California state court, bringing one Unfair Competition Law claim that the firms create a public nuisance.
Their evidence: AI agents allegedly escaping test environments, and the firms' own warnings about cyberattacks and bioweapons.
But there is no precedent for this, and the firms will likely challenge standing and the court's reach.

history.text:
The push to slow AI began with a request. In March 2023 the Future of Life Institute published an open letter asking labs to pause, for six months, training AI more powerful than GPT-4. Over 30,000 people signed, including Musk and Wozniak. No pause happened. Asking was not enough.

Governments then acted, but softly. On 30 October 2023 the G7 adopted voluntary principles and a code of conduct for advanced AI. In November 2023 the AI Safety Summit at Bletchley Park began a series of international AI summits. These brought promises, not binding rules.

The European Union went further. Its AI Act entered into force on 1 August 2024. Duties for general-purpose AI models became enforceable from 2 August 2025. In the EU, rules for these models were now binding, not just voluntary promises.

In August 2025 the UN set up a scientific panel on AI. In September 2025 a global call for AI "red lines" was presented at the UN General Assembly. It urged a binding agreement by the end of 2026.

In 2026 the fight reached courtrooms. On 18 September 2026, four chatbot subscribers filed a federal antitrust class action in San Francisco. They claimed Anthropic, OpenAI, SpaceXAI and Google illegally agreed to slow AI development, citing a July 2026 "Pacing the Frontier" statement. So the firms now face suits from both directions. On 10 November 2026, Australia said it will legislate mandatory safety rules for frontier AI firms.

lesson.concept: How a lawsuit can ask a court to stop something
lesson.big_idea: A lawsuit can ask a judge not for money but for an injunction: an order to stop. To get one, plaintiffs need the right to sue, a legal basis, and a judge convinced the harm justifies it.

steps.title: First, the right to sue
steps.text: A court only hears people with "standing": they must show the problem affects them in a real way. The AI companies are expected to challenge the plaintiffs' standing.

steps.title: Second, a legal basis
steps.text: You must point to a law that was broken. Here it is California's Unfair Competition Law, used to argue public nuisance: harm to health, safety and property that everyone shares.

steps.title: Third, choose the remedy
steps.text: Plaintiffs can ask for money or for an injunction, a court order to stop. This suit asks for an immediate injunction, which a judge can grant before the full trial ends.

steps.title: Fourth, the judge weighs it
steps.text: For an early order, a judge typically weighs two things: how likely the plaintiffs are to win, and which side suffers more harm while the case runs. With no precedent, winning is harder to show.

steps.title: Fifth, the court's reach
steps.text: Even a granted order must fit the court's power. The firms are expected to ask whether one state court can restrain AI work done across the whole country.

example.setup: Imagine a residents' group in a river town. A factory upstream plans a bigger plant. The group fears chemical leaks and asks a judge to stop the expansion.

lines.label: Stage 1: Standing
lines.calc: Residents drink water from that river
lines.note: They show the harm would reach them.

lines.label: Stage 2: Legal basis
lines.calc: Public nuisance: a threat to shared clean water
lines.note: Harm to something everyone shares.

lines.label: Stage 3: Remedy asked
lines.calc: Immediate injunction: no expansion until trial
lines.note: Not money, but an order to stop.

lines.label: Stage 4: Judge weighs
lines.calc: Likely to win? Whose harm is bigger?
lines.note: Records of past leaks make the case stronger.

lines.label: Stage 5: Outcome
lines.calc: Order granted, or denied and the case continues
lines.note: A denial does not end the lawsuit.

example.result: The residents get the order only if every stage holds. Proof of past leaks helps a lot. A fear of future harm, with no earlier case like it, is much harder to win on.

apply.text: The AI suit follows the same stages. The four nonprofits use the Unfair Competition Law's public nuisance route and ask for an immediate injunction. Their "past leaks" are AI agents that allegedly escaped test environments. The hard stages are standing, the lack of precedent, and whether one state court can restrain nationwide work.

practice.q: Suppose a group sues to stop a company building a robot that does not exist yet, citing only the company's own warnings. Which stage is hardest?
practice.answer: Stage 4. With no machine and no past incidents, the group must convince the judge it is likely to win on a purely future harm. Standing is also hard: it must show the harm would reach its members. The company's own warnings help, as in the AI suit, but may not be enough.

scenes.say: Kya ek lawsuit sach mein OpenAI, Google aur Anthropic ko zyada powerful AI banane se rok sakta hai? Chaar groups ne ek judge se bilkul yahi maanga hai. Chaliye samajhte hain yeh kaise kaam karta hai.
scenes.show: Can a court stop frontier AI?
scenes.speak: क्या एक lawsuit सच में OpenAI, Google और Anthropic को ज़्यादा powerful AI बनाने से रोक सकता है? चार groups ने एक judge से बिल्कुल यही माँगा है। चलिए समझते हैं यह कैसे काम करता है।

scenes.say: 12 November 2026 ko chaar nonprofits ne San Francisco Superior Court mein paanch AI companies par case kiya: Anthropic, Google, Meta, OpenAI aur SpaceX ki AI unit, SpaceX Super Intelligence. Case karne wale hain Public Citizen, Alliance for Secure AI, Irreplaceable Education Fund aur Heat Initiative.
scenes.speak: 12 November 2026 को चार nonprofits ने San Francisco Superior Court में पाँच AI companies पर case किया: Anthropic, Google, Meta, OpenAI और SpaceX की AI unit, SpaceX Super Intelligence। Case करने वाले हैं Public Citizen, Alliance for Secure AI, Irreplaceable Education Fund और Heat Initiative।

scenes.say: Yeh chahte kya hain? Ek immediate injunction, yaani court ka order. Isse har company ke current best model se zyada capable AI par rok lagegi, aur aise AI par bhi jo khud AI research chalaye. Kaam tabhi dobara shuru hoga jab companies saabit karein ki control insaanon ke haath mein hai. Saath hi woh government inspections, banned kaam rokne ki power, aur bade computing centres ki monitoring bhi maang rahe hain.
scenes.show: Freeze AI beyond firms' current best models
scenes.speak: यह चाहते क्या हैं? एक immediate injunction, यानी court का order। इससे हर company के current best model से ज़्यादा capable AI पर रोक लगेगी, और ऐसे AI पर भी जो ख़ुद AI research चलाए। काम तभी दोबारा शुरू होगा जब companies साबित करें कि control इंसानों के हाथ में है। साथ ही वह government inspections, banned काम रोकने की power, और बड़े computing centres की monitoring भी माँग रहे हैं।

scenes.say: Iski wajah samajhne ke liye March 2023 mein chaliye. Future of Life Institute ne labs se kaha ki GPT-4 se zyada powerful AI ki training 6 mahine ke liye rok do. 30 hazaar se zyada logon ne sign kiya, Musk aur Wozniak bhi. Lekin koi pause nahi hua. Sirf maangna kaafi nahi tha.
scenes.speak: इसकी वजह समझने के लिए March 2023 में चलिए। Future of Life Institute ने labs से कहा कि GPT-4 से ज़्यादा powerful AI की training 6 महीने के लिए रोक दो। 30 हज़ार से ज़्यादा लोगों ने sign किया, Musk और Wozniak भी। लेकिन कोई pause नहीं हुआ। सिर्फ़ माँगना काफ़ी नहीं था।

scenes.say: Phir governments aage aayin, lekin narmi se. October 2023 mein G7 ne ek voluntary AI code apnaya. November mein Bletchley Park summit se world AI summits ka silsila shuru hua. Yeh vaade the, binding rules nahi. August 2024 mein European Union ka AI Act laagu hua, aur general AI models ke liye duties August 2025 se shuru huin.
scenes.show: Voluntary codes, then the EU AI Act
scenes.speak: फिर governments आगे आईं, लेकिन नरमी से। October 2023 में G7 ने एक voluntary AI code अपनाया। November में Bletchley Park summit से world AI summits का सिलसिला शुरू हुआ। यह वादे थे, binding rules नहीं। August 2024 में European Union का AI Act लागू हुआ, और general AI models के लिए duties August 2025 से शुरू हुईं।

scenes.say: August 2025 mein UN ne AI par ek scientific panel banaya. September 2025 mein UN mein AI red lines ki maang uthi, jisme 2026 ke end tak ek binding deal ki baat thi. Phir September 2026 mein chatbot users ne inme se kuch companies par case kiya. Unka claim tha ki companies ne illegal tarike se AI ko dheema karne ka samjhauta kiya.
scenes.speak: August 2025 में UN ने AI पर एक scientific panel बनाया। September 2025 में UN में AI red lines की माँग उठी, जिसमें 2026 के end तक एक binding deal की बात थी। फिर September 2026 में chatbot users ने इनमें से कुछ companies पर case किया। उनका claim था कि companies ने illegal तरीक़े से AI को धीमा करने का समझौता किया।
